body:
Hi, thanks for maintaining chalk - it is one of the most widely used and best-kept small libraries in the ecosystem, and that reputation is exactly why we picked it for a full-rigor audit: not to hunt for problems, but to see whether a genuinely well-run project comes back clean. At HEAD `aa06bb5` (chalk 5.6.2, Node 22.18.0) the core library did come back clean on architecture, security, and correctness - `npm test` was green (32/32 ava tests, 99.61 percent statement coverage), xo and tsd both passed. One correctness bug turned up anyway, in the public API, and it seems worth your time: at color level 1, `ansi256()`/`bgAnsi256()` emit raw 256-color escape codes instead of downsampling to ANSI-16 the way `rgb()`/`hex()` already do. The suite did not catch it in part because that code path had zero test coverage before this audit (index.js lines 90-91 were never exercised); once coverage was added, a follow-up pass surfaced the downconversion gap itself. We have a small patch and a regression test ready, and we are glad to share it here or open a PR, whichever is easier on your end.

### `ansi256()`/`bgAnsi256()` don't downsample at level 1 (Medium, correctness)

Readme line 228 states: "Colors are downsampled from 16 million RGB values to an ANSI color format that is supported by the terminal emulator (or by specifying `{level: n}` as a Chalk option)." That holds for `rgb()` and `hex()`, but not for `ansi256()`/`bgAnsi256()`.

```
node -e "const {Chalk} = require('chalk'); const c = new Chalk({level: 1}); console.log(JSON.stringify(c.ansi256(196)('x')))"
```

At level 1 this prints `"\^[[38;5;196mx\^[[39m"` - the raw 256-color code, which a level-1 terminal does not support - while the equivalent call through the rgb model, `new Chalk({level: 1}).rgb(255, 0, 0)('x')`, correctly downsamples to `"\^[[91mx\^[[39m"`. `bgAnsi256(196)` shows the same gap against `bgRgb(255, 0, 0)` (raw `48;5;196` instead of the downsampled `101`). Level 2 and level 3 output is unaffected either way; this is specific to level-1 (basic, 16-color) terminals.

Root cause: in `source/index.js`, `getModelAnsi` branches the `rgb` model on level - `ansi16m` gets full truecolor, `ansi256` gets `rgbToAnsi256`, and anything else (level 1) gets downsampled further via `rgbToAnsi` - and the `hex` model redirects into that same `rgb` branch. The `ansi256` model has no such branch at all: every call falls through to the function's final, unconditional line, `ansiStyles[type][model](...arguments_)`, i.e. `ansiStyles[type].ansi256(...)`, regardless of level. `ansiStyles.ansi256ToAnsi` already exists in the vendored ansi-styles package and is exactly the conversion the `rgb` branch's own downsample step uses in spirit. The fix is one additional branch in `getModelAnsi`, checked before that fallback, mirroring the shape of the existing rgb-to-ansi branch: when `model === 'ansi256'` and `level === 'ansi'`, return `ansiStyles[type].ansi(ansiStyles.ansi256ToAnsi(...arguments_))` instead of falling through. With that branch in place, `ansi256(196)` at level 1 emits `"\^[[91m...\^[[39m"` and `bgAnsi256(196)` emits `"\^[[101m...\^[[49m"`, matching the rgb/hex behavior; level 2 and level 3 passthrough is unchanged.

The rest of what the audit found and fixed sits entirely in the tooling perimeter around the library, not the library itself: a dead `benchmark.js` that imported a file that no longer exists and depended on an abandoned `matcha` package, 12 to 14 known vulnerabilities in the xo/ava dev-dependency chains (zero in the shipped runtime, which has no runtime dependencies at all), the ansi256 test-coverage gap mentioned above, and a CI matrix that only tested EOL Node versions (14/16/18) with a deprecated `codecov-action@v2`. All of that is fixed in the same patch if you want it, but we want to be clear the core library came through the full audit clean, which given chalk's reputation was the result we expected going in.

### What we have ready

A patch against `aa06bb5` (`source/index.js`, `test/chalk.js`, plus the tooling-perimeter changes above - 6 files, +76/-67, excluding the regenerated `package-lock.json`) adds the one `getModelAnsi` branch and a regression test covering `ansi256` and `bgAnsi256` at level 1, and confirms level 2/3 output is unchanged. With the full patch applied: 34/34 tests passing, 100 percent statement coverage, `npm audit` at 0 vulnerabilities. We are happy to attach or link the patch, whichever is easier for you to review.

This finding comes out of a documented audit run - journal, patch, and report are published at https://github.com/lenamonj/jeffy-loop/tree/main/evals/chalk - and it was reproduced and reviewed by a human before we filed this.

If it would help, we are glad to open a PR for just the `ansi256`/`bgAnsi256` fix, or for the wider tooling patch, whichever you would prefer - and happy to follow any contribution conventions you would like us to use.
title: ansi256()/bgAnsi256() skip ANSI-16 downsampling at level 1, unlike rgb()/hex() (patch and regression test ready)

body:
chalk has 445M weekly downloads and a single npm account with publish access. It also has no OIDC provenance.

Three packages with the same structural profile were compromised since March:

- **axios** (Mar 30) — stolen npm token, malicious version pushed to latest
- **TanStack** (May 11) — GitHub Actions cache poisoning extracted OIDC tokens, 84 malicious versions in 6 minutes
- **@redhat-cloud-services** (Jun 1) — compromised GitHub account triggered existing CI, 32 packages with valid SLSA provenance built malware

npm's Staged Publishing (GA May 2026) adds a human 2FA approval step between `npm publish` and the version hitting `latest`. If a token is stolen, the attacker's version sits in a holding area instead of going live immediately.

Andrey Sitnik adopted it on nanoid and nanospy after the TanStack incident. PostCSS is next, per [postcss/postcss#2096](https://github.com/postcss/postcss/issues/2096).

**Concrete steps:**

1. Replace `npm publish` with `npm stage publish`
2. Approve with 2FA: `npm promote chalk@<version> latest`
3. Or use the `@npm/staged-publish` GitHub Action for CI-driven releases with manual approval

This doesn't add friction to the development workflow — only to the publish step. One stolen credential no longer means instant deployment to 445M installs/week.
title: Staged Publishing — 445M weekly downloads, sole npm publisher, no provenance

body:
## Summary

The `createBuilder` function uses `arguments_.join(' ')` for multi-argument calls. For the common **2-argument case**, using direct string concatenation instead could provide a **~2.7x speedup**.

## Why is `join()` slow for 2 arguments?

```javascript
arguments_.join(' ')  // Current
```
- Array iteration (even for just 2 items)
- Method dispatch overhead

```javascript
arguments_[0] + ' ' + arguments_[1]  // Faster alternative
```
- V8 primitive operation, JIT-inlined

## Use Case

The 2-argument pattern is common:

```javascript
chalk.red('Error:', message)
chalk.blue('Count:', count)
chalk.green('User:', username)
```

## Environment

- Node.js: v20+
- chalk: 5.6.2
- OS: macOS (Apple M1)

Happy to submit a PR with benchmarks if this optimization is welcome!
title: perf: 2.7x speedup for 2-argument calls using string concat instead of join()

I'm migrating to chalk v5 and see that the `.keyword` function is gone (with the suggestion to use the `color-convert` library as a replacement).  That's all fine, but unless I'm missing something I'm not seeing any way to use the ANSI names along with the `color-convert` library to replicate the named colors within chalk.

For example, if I have the given line:
```js
console.log(chalk.bold.blue('Hello world!'));
```
and I want to be able to use a dynamic color I would previously under chalk 4.x used:
```js
const mycolor = "green"; // or any other color
console.log(chalk.bold.keyword(mycolor)('Hello world!'));
```
How are we supposed to achieve the same flexibility with chalk v5? I see that I can use a `keyword` function with `color-convert` but that uses CSS color names, not ANSI names.  If I have to manually determine equivalent CSS color names or actual RGB values it would appear that (at least for dynamic color names) a lot of usefulness is gone from chalk.

Maybe I'm missing something simple?  I just want to be able to still directly use the chalk color name functions but also occasionally specify a color name dynamically.
title: Using dynamic color names in chalk v5

Hello, since the original issue https://github.com/chalk/chalk/issues/656 was locked, I am making a new one here.

To ensure proper followup by all users of this library, it's important that a security advisory gets published that can get picked up by automated software composition analysis tools like Dependency Track. Unless I missed it, this has not happened for chalk unlike the other packages involved in the breach that I checked. Currently people can only find out that they installed the malicious package by manually checking if they have the malicious version or not.

Creating a security advisory can be done by requesting a CVE at the NVD and/or by creating a GitHub Security Advisory in this repository.
title: Security advisory for malicious package publication
